transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-09-14 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Reed (Redwood SE), Eric Huang (Redwood Solutions), Priya Sharma (Halo Head of Platform), Liam O'Connell (Lead ML Eng), Rosa Martinez (Security Architect)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Halo Analytics evaluating Redwood for hybrid onramp - they want hosted for dev, dedicated for prod, private/vpc for regulated subsets. Main topics: SDK integration with LangChain/LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy pattern, rate limits/quotas and token accounting, observability hooks and tracing, SOC2/KMS requirements. Next step pilot + security docs + benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00:05] Maya Patel: hey everybody, thanks for joining. is this a good time?
[00:00:12] Priya Sharma: yep thanks, we got 60 minutes set, hoping to cover architecture and next steps.
[00:00:18] Jonas Reed: i can kick off with a quick overview of how redwood typically sits in a stack, then dig into gateway and sdk patterns.
[00:00:25] Liam O'Connell: cool, we've got a few constraints — latency at 95p under 220ms for short queries, and heavy embedding throughput overnight.
[00:00:33] Rosa Martinez: and security is a blocker — we need SSO, KMS integration, audit logs, and possibly private onprem for PHI.
[00:00:40] Eric Huang: understood. quick callout, we support hosted for early testing, dedicated reserved pools for steady production, and private deploy with VPC or on-prem packaging.
[00:00:52] Priya Sharma: can you clarify the private deploy — is it a turn-key appliance or something we have to stitch?
[00:00:59] Jonas Reed: it's customer-managed control plane option. basically the same api surface, but control plane runs in your VPC; on-prem is an optional bundle with local runtime. there are some ops pieces but we provide automation scripts.
[00:01:10] [00:01:15] Liam O'Connell: how about SDKs — we use LangChain heavily and a few LlamaIndex notebooks for R&D. what's the recommended integration path?
[00:01:22] Maya Patel: we have first-class SDKs in python/node, and connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. typical pattern is keep a small gateway inside your infra that does auth, routing and can enforce rate limits before hitting redwood.
[00:01:35] Jonas Reed: yeah the gateway/proxy can be as light as an envoy filter or our provided sidecar. it handles api-key translation, header enrichment with tenant ids, basic batching and local prefix caching to reduce calls.
[00:01:47] Priya Sharma: hm "local prefix caching" — do you mean KV cache? we've seen mention of K V cash in other docs...
[00:01:53] Jonas Reed: sorry yeah, KV cache, sometimes transcribed weird by the tooling — we keep token-level kv caches for chat workloads which drastically reduce repeated token decode cost.
[00:02:05] [00:02:12] Rosa Martinez: important for us: encryption at rest and in transit, KMS integration, and clear audit trails. do you have SOC2 stuff?
[00:02:18] Maya Patel: we do. we'll share SOC 2 type 2 and ISO attestation, plus an architecture diagram showing KMS and HSM options. also SAML/SSO and SCIM for provisioning.
[00:02:30] Liam O'Connell: for quotas — we expect spikes; do you do token-based quotas or request-level quotas?
[00:02:38] Jonas Reed: both. per-tenant token quota is typical for hosted; dedicated can have capacity-based throughput and you can set per-route quotas. also burst policies for short spikes.
[00:02:49] Priya Sharma: what about cost predictability — we're worried about sudden token storms from bad prompts.
[00:02:55] Eric Huang: you can configure per-route hard caps and soft warnings. theres also usage hooks in the console so you can tie alerts to token burn. and we provide suggestions via Optimize for quantization and batching to reduce unit cost.
[00:03:09] [00:03:20] Liam O'Connell: the LangChain integration — does redwood pencil into the LLM wrappers or do we call the SDK directly?
[00:03:26] Jonas Reed: both options: you can use our LLM wrapper that's LangChain-compatible or call the SDK directly if you want custom retry and routing logic. the wrapper sets sensible defaults for streaming and function calling.
[00:03:37] Priya Sharma: any known issues with LlamaIndex? we rely on some index-based reranking and hybrid search.
[00:03:44] Maya Patel: LlamaIndex works fine, but watch for consistent embeddings. we recommend pinning the embedding model and enabling deterministic tokenizers when rehydrating indices. sometimes tokenizer mismatch causes drift.
[00:03:55] Rosa Martinez: about observability — we need tracing hooks integrated into our APM and also per-request token breakdown. is there a distributed trace header passthrough?
[00:04:03] Jonas Reed: yes we accept W3C traceparent headers and propagate them through the runtime. the console surfaces per-request token count, model, latency breakdown (generation vs decode), and you can export telemetry via OTLP to your observability stack.
[00:04:17] Liam O'Connell: perfect — we use DataDock and Lightbristle (internal APM names changed) so OTLP is enough.
[00:04:23] [00:04:30] Priya Sharma: network topology question — if we run a gateway in our VPC to the hosted redwood endpoint, do we send customer data over public internet?
[00:04:38] Eric Huang: for hosted, traffic goes over TLS to our public ingress; for private you can have peering or private link options. dedicated also supports private peering on certain cloud providers.
[00:04:50] Rosa Martinez: what's the SLA for dedicated vs hosted?
[00:04:55] Maya Patel: hosted has best-effort latency targets, dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency SLOs depending on contract tier. private is negotiable as part of the enterprise license.
[00:05:06] [00:05:12] Liam O'Connell: about benchmarking — our 95p needs to be measured end-to-end from our gateway through the runtime. can redwood run a benchmark using our sample payloads?
[00:05:19] Jonas Reed: yes SEs do benchmark runs. we'll need representative prompts, batch sizes, sequence lengths, and whether you're using embeddings or chat. we can run with compatible model variants and provide a report with CPU/GPU utilization, p95/p99 latency, and cost per 1M tokens.
[00:05:37] Priya Sharma: do you have model variants that trade accuracy vs cost?
[00:05:41] Jonas Reed: we expose lighter quantized variants and recommend them for throughput-heavy workloads. Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization levels and batching configs by workload.
[00:05:51] [00:06:00] Rosa Martinez: auditor question — we need immutable logs for all inference requests for 90 days. is that available?
[00:06:07] Eric Huang: yes you can ship request logs to an object store under your control, or we can retain them under our retention policy if you need. for regulated data we strongly recommend sending logs to your own S3 with server-side encryption.
[00:06:20] Liam O'Connell: any caveats with embedding pipelines — we plan to precompute embeddings nightly and also do on-demand rerank. does the platform support bulk embedding jobs?
[00:06:28] Jonas Reed: we support async bulk embedding jobs and streaming subsets for nearline. the embedding endpoints have bulk APIs with parallel workers; for very large jobs we recommend dedicated capacity to avoid noisy neighbor issues.
[00:06:40] [00:06:48] Priya Sharma: how does rate-limiting interact with batching and caching? if gateway aggregates requests for batching, does that bypass per-user quotas?
[00:06:57] Jonas Reed: batching happens at the runtime layer and respects token quotas. the gateway can aggregate to increase throughput but the token accounting is still per-origin/tenant. if you use shared gateway, you must propagate tenant id so quotas map correctly.
[00:07:12] Rosa Martinez: about tenant isolation — in dedicated pools can we pin a tenant to a hardware pool?
[00:07:18] Maya Patel: yes dedicated pools are effectively reserved hardware; you can pin workloads and even restrict which model versions are accessible.
[00:07:25] [00:07:31] Liam O'Connell: we have a crazy evening batch that spikes to 10k requests per minute for embeddings — will dedicated handle that with autoscaling?
[00:07:40] Jonas Reed: dedicated supports autoscaling within your reserved capacity and burst capacity on top for short windows. we can size the pool for your nightly peak or set burst provisioning; pricing differs.
[00:07:52] Priya Sharma: for prototyping we'd like hosted, but for production keys and data we need private for a subset of customers — is hybrid routing supported?
[00:07:59] Eric Huang: absolutely. smart routing policies let you send requests by tenant or route to hosted/dedicated/private. we also support automatic fallback when a target is saturated.
[00:08:12] [00:08:20] Liam O'Connell: can we do A/B deployments across model versions? we want canary and automatic rollback on quality regressions.
[00:08:28] Jonas Reed: rollouts are supported: canary, weight-based, and automatic fallback policies. we also tie quality regression alerts to prompt sets so you can detect hallucination spikes vs token drift.
[00:08:41] Priya Sharma: any gotchas integrating with our infra-as-code?
[00:08:45] Maya Patel: we provide terraform modules and helm charts; the private on-prem package includes ansible playbooks. some customers customize init scripts for the gateway sidecar.
[00:08:58] [00:09:05] Rosa Martinez: one nit: how do you handle secret rotation for keys used by the gateway?
[00:09:09] Jonas Reed: we integrate with KMS/HSM and support short-lived tokens. gateways can request ephemeral credentials via a vault or STS flow.
[00:09:18] Liam O'Connell: practical question — for our LangChain agents that do tool calling, we need streaming chunked responses and function call semantics preserved. does the SDK support server-sent events or streaming websockets?
[00:09:28] Jonas Reed: yes streaming via chunked http and websockets is supported. the LangChain wrapper maps streaming chunks into the iterator pattern LangChain expects and function calls are supported in structured output mode.
[00:09:42] [00:09:50] Priya Sharma: okay, jumping to observability — can we get per-route token attribution and hook into our tracing so we get single view in DataDock?
[00:09:58] Eric Huang: yes, you can export OTLP traces and we provide a token-breakdown export. our console also has a token explorer for quick queries.
[00:10:10] Liam O'Connell: great. when do you think we can run a proof-of-concept?
[00:10:14] Maya Patel: if you share payloads and sign an NDA (if needed), we can spin up hosted test keys within 2 business days and run an SE-led benchmark within a week.
[00:10:24] Priya Sharma: we do need an NDA for certain datasets, i'll coordinate with legal.
[00:10:30] [00:10:36] Jonas Reed: one more technical detail — if you use the gateway sidecar, we can enable local request coalescing for identical requests which reduces immediate spikes to the runtime. it is usually safe for idempotent calls but not for messages with user-specific state.
[00:10:52] Rosa Martinez: curious about delete/retention — if a tenant requests deletion of PII, how is that handled across cached kv and logs?
[00:11:00] Jonas Reed: we have data lifecycle APIs; you can purge tenant data from KV cache and request log export and deletion. note there's propagation time across replicas so meeting our retention SLA requires pipeline work which SE will help define.
[00:11:15] [00:11:22] Priya Sharma: thank you. i want to surface a small compliance checklist: SOC2, encryption, immutable logs, private peering, SAML, data deletion API.
[00:11:32] Maya Patel: we'll include a checklist in the pack we send.
[00:11:36] [00:11:42] Liam O'Connell: pricing — do you offer committed spend discounts for dedicated?
[00:11:46] Maya Patel: yes monthly/annual committed capacity discounts exist, and enterprise contracts bundle private deployments and premium support.
[00:11:55] Priya Sharma: any reference customers in healthcare or finance?
[00:11:58] Eric Huang: we can provide redacted references; i'll add those to the pack.
[00:12:04] [00:12:10] Jonas Reed: do you want us to propose a sizing for dedicated vs hosted for your workload?
[00:12:15] Priya Sharma: yes please, include cost vs latency tradeoffs and a recommended pilot size.
[00:12:21] [00:12:28] Maya Patel: action: we'll send security docs, topology and a pilot proposal. SE will ask for the sample prompts and the nightly embedding batch profile.
[00:12:36] [00:12:40] Priya Sharma: okay that's helpful. one more question on rate-limits: we have multi-tenant customers within Halo; can we have quota hierarchies (org -> tenant -> user)?
[00:12:49] Jonas Reed: yes quotas are hierarchical; you can set global org limits, and then allocate to tenants and users. the console helps visualize burn-down.
[00:12:58] [00:13:05] Liam O'Connell: are there any pitfalls with using the LangChain wrapper for agents that call external tools?
[00:13:12] Jonas Reed: main thing is ensure your tool-calling flow is idempotent or guarded, because retries can cause duplicate tool invocations. we provide idempotency keys for that purpose.
[00:13:24] Priya Sharma: let's talk timeline — our Q4 roadmap targets a soft launch for a subset of customers in mid-November.
[00:13:32] Maya Patel: realistic: pilot in late September/early October, iterate through 4 weeks, then plan dedicated sizing and procurement in October to hit mid-November.
[00:13:43] Rosa Martinez: procurement will need contract and security addendum, and possibly a reviewed SOC2 report.
[00:13:50] Maya Patel: understood.
[00:13:54] [00:14:00] Jonas Reed: quick note about plugin/tool calling — for outbound webhooks to your toolchain we can offer egress restrictions and VPC NAT rules so calls originate from known IP ranges.
[00:14:11] Liam O'Connell: good. i'm curious about per-token cost for embeddings vs chat — ballpark numbers?
[00:14:18] Eric Huang: we'll include pricing scenarios in the proposal; embeddings are typically cheaper per token but you pay for storage and retrieval at scale. we'll break it down in the spreadsheet.
[00:14:29] [00:14:35] Priya Sharma: anything else we should know about upgrade paths between hosted -> dedicated -> private? is there downtime?
[00:14:43] Jonas Reed: generally no downtime; it's routing changes and potentially migrating keys and model pinning. we support blue-green migrations and can assist SE-side.
[00:14:55] [00:15:02] Maya Patel: alright let's recap next steps: send security pack, sample prompts and batching profile, schedule pilot kickoff, SE benchmark plan.
[00:15:11] Priya Sharma: agreed. liaise with my PM Sam for scheduling.
[00:15:16] [00:15:22] Jonas Reed: i'll put together a benchmark checklist — payload shapes, concurrency, token lengths, expected QPS.
[00:15:29] Liam O'Connell: i'll export our traffic traces to share.
[00:15:33] Rosa Martinez: i'll coordinate legal for NDA and contract questions.
[00:15:38] [00:15:45] Maya Patel: thanks everyone — we will follow up with the deck and docs.
[00:15:50] Priya Sharma: thanks, appreciated.

[00:16:00] Meeting end notes (auto): approximate timestamps after 15 minutes reflect the main scoping. remaining time was Q&A on observability and security nuances and confirming pilot dates.
